_meta.description: A free, open-source Bible for iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch. Read offline in the ASV, BSB or KJV, study with cross-references, commentary and maps, listen, take sermon notes, share verse images, and sync privately through your own iCloud — no ads, no trackers, no accounts.
_title: Scripture Alone - A Free, Private Bible
a-free-open-source.93993c: A free, open-source Bible for iPhone, iPad and Mac, with its own Apple Watch app. The American Standard Version is on your device from the start and two more translations are a single download away, so you can read, study, listen and take notes anywhere in the world — with or without a connection.
a-toggle-away-tap.8c147a: A toggle away: tap a verse and the Study panel follows, with ranked cross-references (one tap there and back) and classic commentary from John Calvin, John Gill and Jamieson‑Fausset‑Brown. The commentary downloads the first time you open it; cross-references are there from the start.
a-verse-shared-from.c15b16: A verse shared from Scripture Alone
auto-scroll-keeps-the.e753e5: Auto-scroll keeps the text moving at your pace and carries on into the next chapter — an accessibility feature for anyone who finds scrolling by hand difficult, or simply wants to read without touching the screen.
being-built-now-and.f37881: Being built now, and not in the app yet. They'll ship when they're ready.
blaine-miller-all-rights.b327c2: © Blaine Miller. All rights reserved.
browse-the-openly-licensed.da6cd3: Browse the openly licensed translations eBible.org publishes, in your own language first, and download only the ones you choose — or open a USFM file or a DRM-free ePub you already own. The ESV, CSB, NKJV and NASB can't be given away by anyone, so they're read with your own free key from the publisher. Licenses to carry those offline are still being sought.
can-i-add-another-translation.4b1e7a: Can I add another translation myself?
design-a-verse-image.0a20c5: Design a verse image on your device from eight templates, or send a link that rebuilds the card in any browser from the link itself — nothing is stored on a server.
does-it-work-on.d22ae5: Does it work on Apple Watch?
each-chapter-s-era.4b0bd3: Each chapter's era on a timeline of the biblical periods, an offline map of the places it names, and charts of the kings of Israel and Judah, Paul's journeys, the twelve tribes and the feasts of Israel.
every-line-of-code.0797fb: Every line of code is public under the AGPL-3.0 license. Read it, check it, or build it yourself.
everything-here-works-today.40d987: Everything here works today, on the device in your hand.
free-forever-no-ads.ca5514: Free forever. No ads, no trackers, no accounts. Built to help people study God's word and grow closer to Christ.
hear-any-chapter-read.f4ef56: Hear any chapter read aloud with your device's voices, Premium and Personal Voice included, the spoken verse marked as it goes, with a sleep timer and lock-screen controls. On iPhone and iPad, Mi Speaks subscribers can hand a chapter to its Studio voices.
highlight-in-five-colors.0d2ff8: Highlight in five colors, heart the verses you return to, and attach a note to one or more passages — a Sunday sermon on Romans 8:1–17, say. Export your notes as a PDF, Markdown or plain text.
how-do-share-links.af837c: How do share links work? Is my verse sent anywhere?
is-scripture-alone-available.8b64bc: Is Scripture Alone available in the European Union?
it-s-a-careful.2cd1ba: It's a careful, word-for-word translation in the public domain, so it can be given away freely — the Berean Standard Bible and King James Version are included for the same reason. Translations like the CSB, ESV, NKJV and NASB need publisher licenses, which we're requesting.
layouts-that-know-about.4b0f61: Layouts that know about the fold, so the text and the Study panel make the most of iPhone Duo's larger screen.
make-a-keepsake-of.5d6bbd: Make a keepsake of your highlights and notes for your family: one file, optionally protected with a passphrase, that they open and read as you marked it — a digital “Dad's Bible” to hand down.
no-ads-no-analytics.490c17: No ads. No analytics. No third-party SDKs. Your notes travel only through your own iCloud.
no-google-play-download.8a9d61: No Google Play? Download the APK from GitHub, with every translation and study tool built in. It doesn't update itself, and it can't be updated by the Google Play version, so read the notes there first.
none-there-are-no.762c80: None. There are no analytics, no trackers and no accounts. Your highlights and notes stay on your devices and sync only through your own private iCloud, which I can't see.
nothing-between-you-and.27b4f3: Nothing between you and the text
photograph-the-sermon-slide.813c96: Photograph the sermon slide and on-device text recognition starts your note: titled from the slide, linked to every passage on it, its points ready as bullets. The photo is discarded unless you keep it.
put-any-two-side.7c4144: Put any two side by side, verse for verse, and see where they part company — including a translation you read online with your own key.
set-the-way-it.444ce2: Set the way it was written
seven-typefaces-adjustable-size.16f95c: Seven typefaces, adjustable size and line spacing, five themes — Auto, Light, Sepia, Dark and Black — and an accent color of your choosing. Read in paragraphs or verse by verse, with full Dynamic Type support.
share-your-notes-and.6116ef: Share your notes and highlights with family as you keep adding to them, not only as a keepsake file.
tap-a-verse-for.021f01: Tap a verse for the Hebrew or Greek behind it, word by word, with parsing, Strong's numbers and a lexicon entry for each. It works in every translation, and downloads once the first time you open it.
the-american-standard-version.331aee: The American Standard Version is on your device from the moment the app installs, so it reads offline before you ever connect. The Berean Standard Bible and the King James Version download once, the first time you choose one, and are yours offline from then on. All three are public domain, with full-text search.
the-american-standard-version.ebc980: The American Standard Version ships sealed: signed by a key the app pins, decrypted a chapter at a time, searchable without its text ever lying in the open on your device. It's the format a publisher's own translation would travel in — read how it works.
the-link-carries-the.8f367c: The link carries the verse itself, after the “#” in the address. Browsers never send that part to a server, so this site never sees what you shared: the page rebuilds the card right in the browser. If Scripture Alone is installed, the link opens the passage in the app instead.
the-word-and-nothing.59b9cc: The Word, and nothing in the way.
the-words-of-christ.c6c665: The words of Christ in red, section headings, poetry laid out as poetry, and footnotes a tap away.
this-card-was-rebuilt.8b3b06: This card was rebuilt in your browser from the link itself. The verse was never sent to a server.
this-link-needs-a.35b383: This link needs a newer version of the page.
this-passage-is-too.ce073d: This passage is too long to show from a link.
this-share-link-is.5d635d: This share link is incomplete or damaged, so its verse can't be shown.
to-join-join-the.9646c8: To join, join the beta group, then opt in on Google Play with the same Google account and install it from there. If Google Play says the test isn't available yet, the first build is still in Google's review, so try again in a day or two.
type-jn-3-16.ee05d2: Type “jn 3 16” or “rom 8:28-39” to jump to a passage, or search for any word or phrase. Recent chapters and recent searches are waiting when you come back.
verse-of-the-day.bc6058: Verse of the Day and Favorites & Notes widgets for the Home and Lock Screens, and an Apple Watch app with the ASV, BSB and KJV offline — it follows the translation you're reading on your iPhone — plus your favorites and notes, and a complication with the day's reference.
years-of-notes-in.6859a3: Years of notes in another Bible app don't have to be left behind. Import a Life Bible (formerly Tecarta) export directly, or paste notes or a CSV from anywhere else. Importing twice is safe — anything already there is left alone.
yes-for-translations-that.0ed3fa: Yes, for translations that are openly licensed. Scripture Alone can open a USFM file or a DRM-free ePub, and it can fetch the free catalogue published by eBible.org when you ask it to, with your own language first — nothing is downloaded unless you tap. Imported translations stay on your device. This is an interim arrangement: requests to license the major modern translations are with their publishers, and if those are granted the translations will simply be in the app, and this may go away.
yes-in-a-closed.b8b573: Yes, in a closed beta on Google Play: a native app for Android phones and tablets, with its own Wear OS app. Your highlights and notes stay on the device, since there's no iCloud on Android.
yes-no-ads-no.bf78fd: Yes. No ads, no in-app purchases, no subscriptions. Scripture Alone is free, and it will stay free.
yes-on-any-mac.d853c7: Yes, on any Mac with Apple silicon. Install the iPad app from the App Store on your Mac, and your highlights and notes sync with your iPhone and iPad through iCloud.
yes-scripture-alone-is.9112b8: Yes. Scripture Alone is on the App Store everywhere in the European Union, France included. The source code is open to everyone on GitHub.
yes-the-full-source.c48195: Yes. The full source is on GitHub under the AGPL-3.0 license.
yes-the-watch-app.14dc16: Yes. The watch app carries its own copies of the American Standard Version, the Berean Standard Bible and the King James Version, so it reads offline even without your iPhone nearby, and it follows the translation you're reading on your iPhone — including one you imported. It has the Verse of the Day, your favorites and notes, can read a passage aloud, and puts the day's reference on your watch face.
your-highlights-notes-and.4c0001: Your highlights, notes and favorites follow you across iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch through your own private iCloud. No account, no server — I never see your data.
